importance_ranking.reason: High visual variation across material types (MS, FRP, PUF panel, PVC) and size classes — buyers use the image to instantly assess build quality, material type, and aesthetic fit with their gate. A flimsy or mismatched-looking cabin is skipped immediately without reading further.

Material and size are non-interchangeable shortlisting criteria — a buyer with a fixed gate footprint and a specific material requirement cannot substitute alternatives. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated.

Price varies substantially with material type and size; Indian B2B buyers (RWAs, facility managers) compare prices aggressively across sellers once material and size match. Price is a primary shortlisting lever in this commoditised mid-market segment.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall exists in this category — the market is fragmented across regional prefab manufacturers and buyers search by spec and price, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Buyers check whether the seller is a manufacturer or trader and whether they deliver to the required location; no branded sub-categories exist among siblings and no brand commands active buyer preference.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Custom or large-format orders may be quoted per sq ft, but per-piece dominates for the standard 4x4 to 8x8 ft security cabin segment. No buyer is confused about this unit.
importance_ranking.reason: Guard cabins are finished structures sold per piece — the unit is entirely implied and no buyer ever questions it.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Material (PVC Panel / MS / GI / FRP / ACP Panel) defines the structural type of the cabin — non-interchangeable across buyer requirements and the single largest driver of price variation.
Size (4x4 ft to 8x8 ft) defines the floor footprint — non-interchangeable with gate dimensions and the second-largest price driver after material.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Flat, single-slope, and double-slope roofs differ in weather drainage and structural load — buyers deploying cabins in high-rainfall regions specify roof type, and sellers need it to confirm fabrication capability and quote accurately.

Whether the cabin is supplied with pre-fitted electrical points (fan, light, switchboard) is a meaningful price differentiator and a common buyer requirement that sellers need to confirm at the listing stage.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Material defines the structural type, durability, insulation level, and price tier — a seller manufacturing only MS cabins cannot supply an FRP requirement, making this the primary routing spec.
Gate footprint is fixed by the buyer's site — size is non-interchangeable and sellers need it to confirm stock availability or fabrication feasibility before responding.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need the roof type to confirm fabrication capability and quote accurately — flat vs sloped roofs differ in material, drainage design, and cost.
Sellers need to know whether electrical points are required to quote the correct configuration — pre-fitted electrical adds cost and requires different internal framing.
